column3: The lift is full of actors in giant hats.
column4: full of 表示裝滿；電梯裡都是戴大帽子的演員。

column3: Choose any film. I don't care; I love them all.
column4: I don't care 表示不介意選哪一部電影。

column3: Go on. Your story is better than this film.
column4: go on 是請對方繼續，這裡請他繼續說故事。

column3: My heart beats fast before every driving lesson.
column4: heart beats fast 描述心跳加速；學開車前緊張符合情境。

column3: Be brave. Your first driving lesson has only one student!
column4: be brave 鼓勵人勇敢；這裡打趣學車時無須面對一大群人。

column3: One more lesson! We're one step closer to the show.
column4: one step closer 表示向目標再接近一步。

column3: Dad shouted “Hello!” and heard it echo inside the cave.
column4: echo 表示聲音迴響；洞內的回音符合用法。

column3: We found a tiny museum along the way to our hotel.
column4: along the way 表示途中；去酒店途中發現博物館。

column3: I returned the extra money. I did what was right.
column4: do what is right 表示做正確、誠實的事。

column3: His smart mouth gets him into trouble at every meeting.
column4: smart mouth 指愛頂嘴或說話放肆，這裡因此在會議上惹麻煩。

column3: I finally pinned Dad down about our holiday dates.
column4: pin someone down 指追問並取得明確答案。

column3: Am I out of my mind to enter this race?
column4: out of my mind 誇張地表示失去理智，這裡懷疑自己是否應參賽。

column3: His great plan is nothing but a name.
column4: nothing but 表示只有；計劃除了名字還沒有內容。

column3: They both collect old maps. Perhaps they're meant to be.
column4: meant to be 在此表示兩人像是天生一對。

column3: That unpaid bill is on my mind again.
column4: on my mind 表示一直惦記；這裡擔心未付帳單。

column3: We're caught in traffic. Even the walkers are winning.
column4: be caught in traffic 指困在車龍；行人走得更快是輕鬆比較。

column3: Borrow my camera as long as you return it.
column4: as long as 表示條件：只要歸還便可借用。

column3: His revenge was simple: he hid his brother's drumsticks.
column4: revenge 指報復；藏起鼓棍是回敬兄弟的小動作。

column3: We've been friends since our first terrible dance class.
column4: be friends 表示是朋友；since 說明友誼的起點。

column3: My fantasy is a robot that attends meetings for me.
column4: fantasy 指想像中的情景；這裡想由機械人代開會。

column3: We escaped from the lift, still holding our party balloons.
column4: escape from 表示逃離被困的地方。

column3: I left my map behind. Our guide looked worried.
column4: leave behind 指把東西遺留在原處。

column3: He's a small-town boy with a big-city haircut.
column4: small-town 作形容詞修飾 boy，表示來自小鎮。

column3: Sit anywhere. The front seats cost nothing today.
column4: anywhere 表示任何地方，這裡可自由選座。

column3: The guide went on and on. We missed the last train.
column4: go on and on 強調說個不停。

column3: Ben walked up and down, practising his interview smile.
column4: up and down 在此表示來回踱步。

column3: Grandma sends me a new dance video every single day.
column4: every single day 強調每天都發生。

column3: The actor took a step onto the king's coat.
column4: take a step 表示踏出一步；這裡不小心踩上戲服。

column3: I faked a smile at my third surprise meeting.
column4: fake a smile 表示裝出笑容，未必真的開心。

column3: My concert ticket vanished without a trace.
column4: without a trace 表示沒有留下蹤跡。

column3: Talking after rehearsal helps us know each other better.
column4: know someone better 表示更了解某人；聊天有助增進了解。

column3: Dad's birthday was in the back of my mind.
column4: in the back of my mind 表示隱約記得或惦記某事。

column3: We talked all night to make up for lost time.
column4: make up for lost time 表示彌補錯過的相處時間。

column3: Nobody hated my speech. It was all in my mind.
column4: all in my mind 表示只是自己的想像。

column3: This jacket keeps me warm during Dad's outdoor speeches.
column4: keep someone warm 表示使人保持溫暖。

column3: I want my old manager back. She understood jokes.
column4: have someone back 的核心意思是讓某人回來；want someone back 表達盼望對方回來。

column3: I shouldn't take Mum for granted. She does so much.
column4: take someone for granted 指把別人的付出視為理所當然。

column3: My sister stood by me after my terrible performance.
column4: stand by someone 指支持某人，尤其在困難時。

column3: My little cousin makes me smile with her funny drawings.
column4: make someone smile 表示使人微笑。

column3: I'd be lost without Mia. She reads every map.
column4: be lost without someone 表示沒有那人幫忙就不知如何應付。

column3: We're apart this week. His dancing can wait.
column4: be apart 指彼此分開，這裡暫時不能一起跳舞。

column3: We made a deal: I drive, you choose the music.
column4: make a deal 表示達成協議，這裡分配開車及選歌的工作。

column3: The trial is free; I've nothing to lose.
column4: nothing to lose 表示試一試也沒有損失。

column3: I've nothing to prove. I can dance badly in peace.
column4: nothing to prove 表示無須向人證明自己，便可自在跳舞。

column3: Make a decision: beach holiday or another museum?
column4: make a decision 表示作出選擇。

column3: We're late. In other words, we missed the parade.
column4: in other words 用另一種說法解釋前面的意思。

column3: Dad filled the room with balloons, then couldn't enter.
column4: fill something with 表示用某物填滿；房間裝滿氣球。

column3: Mum adores that actor, even in his boring films.
column4: adore 表示非常喜愛；媽媽連他的悶電影也看。

column3: We waited for a while. Dad was choosing a seat.
column4: for a while 表示一段時間。

column3: Dad is singing tonight. Expect the worst.
column4: expect the worst 指預料最壞情況，這裡以爸爸的歌聲開玩笑。

column3: Grandma might become a DJ. Never say never!
column4: never say never 表示別斷言事情絕不可能發生。

column3: The manager's tiny party hat made everyone laugh.
column4: make someone laugh 表示使人發笑，這裡是小派對帽的效果。

column3: He forgot my name; I tried not to take it personally.
column4: take it personally 表示把事情視為針對自己；這裡盡量不介意。

column3: He smiled to hide the truth: he'd forgotten our anniversary.
column4: hide the truth 指隱瞞真相；他笑著掩飾忘記紀念日。

column3: You survived three interviews. You deserve a rest.
column4: deserve 表示值得得到；應付多場面試後值得休息。

column3: This meeting feels endless. Even the clock looks tired.
column4: endless 誇張地形容漫長得像沒盡頭的會議。

column3: I believe in Grandma. She can win this race.
column4: believe in someone 指相信對方的能力。

column3: Our hotel is far from the beach. Dad calls it exercise.
column4: far from 表示距離遠；爸爸把長路打趣說成運動。

column3: There's nothing I wouldn't do to help my family.
column4: 雙重否定強調願意盡力幫助家人。

column3: My uncle lives far away but calls during every film.
column4: far away 表示相距遙遠。

column3: I spend time with Grandpa; he teaches me new games.
column4: spend time with someone 表示花時間與人相處。

column3: I sat in front so I wouldn't miss a thing.
column4: miss a thing 表示錯過任何細節。

column3: She held her brother close during the scary film.
column4: hold someone close 表示把人緊緊抱在身邊。

column3: There's no way back now; the boat has left.
column4: no way back 指已無法返回原處或原來狀況。

column3: My camera is brand new. Dad already understands it.
column4: brand new 表示全新，這裡形容相機。

column3: Meeting the queen was a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
column4: once-in-a-lifetime 形容一生難得一次的經歷。

column3: My biggest desire is a holiday without work calls.
column4: desire 是強烈願望；這裡希望假期不受工作電話打擾。

column3: I love crowds; she loves silence. We're two worlds apart.
column4: two worlds apart 形容喜好或想法差異很大。

column3: Too late! The film ended while Dad found his glasses.
column4: too late 表示已經錯過時機。

column3: How did this strange mix-up come to pass?
column4: come to pass 表示發生，這裡問這場誤會如何發生。

column3: She surrounds herself with friends who enjoy terrible jokes.
column4: surround yourself with 指讓某些人常在自己身邊。

column3: He broke his promise and missed our anniversary again.
column4: break a promise 指沒有履行承諾。

column3: My friend pulled me forward through the crowd.
column4: pull someone forward 表示把某人往前拉。

column3: A thousand fans waited. The singer took another exit.
column4: a thousand 表示一千，後接複數 fans。

column3: I came to know my neighbour through our noisy rehearsals.
column4: come to know 表示漸漸認識或了解。

column3: She's a dreamer: she wants a home on the moon.
column4: dreamer 指愛懷抱夢想的人。

column3: Tom is the only one wearing a crown here.
column4: the only one 表示唯一的一人。

column3: She shared her umbrella with our forgetful neighbour.
column4: share something with someone 表示與人共用。

column3: I gave up midnight drumming. My neighbours celebrated.
column4: give up doing something 表示停止某項行為。

column3: I'm fixing the radio right now. It has other plans.
column4: right now 指現在這一刻；收音機好像不肯合作是輕鬆擬人。

column3: Sooner or later, this rain will stop. I hope.
column4: sooner or later 表示遲早會發生。

column3: I feel like visiting the gallery in my bright yellow hat.
column4: feel like doing something 表示想做某事。

column3: At the concert, I was a face in the crowd.
column4: a face in the crowd 指人群中不起眼的一員。

column3: They wanted me to cheat, but I stood my ground.
column4: stand your ground 指堅持自己的立場。

column3: After losing the race, she still stood tall.
column4: stand tall 在此表示保持自信和尊嚴。

column3: I begged my sister to stop sharing my baby photos.
column4: beg someone to do something 表示懇求某人做事。

column3: I forgot our date. I really let her down.
column4: let someone down 表示使人失望。

column3: He turned the map upside down and found our hotel.
column4: turn upside down 表示上下翻轉。

column3: We searched in vain. Dad already had the ring.
column4: in vain 表示徒勞；戒指早在爸爸手中。

column3: She cares for her cousin while his parents travel.
column4: care for someone 在此表示照顧某人。

column3: Marry you? Please let me give it some thought.
column4: give it some thought 表示認真考慮一下。

column3: She shares her taxi with a friend after the late show.
column4: share something with someone 表示與人共用某物。

column3: Who cares if my dance looks silly? It's fun!
column4: Who cares? 在此表示不在乎別人的看法。

column3: Once upon a time, a king feared his own shadow.
column4: once upon a time 用來開始一個發生在從前的故事。

column3: Ben lost his job and wallet. He's down on his luck.
column4: down on your luck 指正在遭遇不順。

column3: I've never acted, but I'll give it a shot.
column4: give it a shot 表示試一試。

column3: Fans watch and wait; the singer uses another exit.
column4: watch and wait 表示一邊留意一邊等候。

column3: Mind over matter helped me finish the freezing swim.
column4: mind over matter 指用意志克服身體的不適。

column3: That awful job chewed him up. He needed rest.
column4: chew someone up 在此形容工作使人身心俱疲。

column3: He wanted to leave, so I let him go.
column4: let someone go 表示允許某人離開。

column3: They wanted me to sing. I wanted to run for the hills.
column4: run for the hills 誇張地表示想趕快逃走。

column3: Dad was worn out after dancing all night.
column4: worn out 在此表示筋疲力盡。

column3: I'm stuck in a cycle of late nights and tired mornings.
column4: stuck in a cycle 指困在不斷重複的模式中。

column3: I was all alone until Grandma called, again.
column4: all alone 表示獨自一人。

column3: The station seems so far when your suitcase has no wheels.
column4: seem so far 表示感覺距離很遠。

column3: They travelled from coast to coast, collecting terrible postcards.
column4: from coast to coast 指從一邊海岸到另一邊海岸。

column3: Five jobs? I've bitten off more than I can chew.
column4: bite off more than you can chew 指承擔超出能力的工作。

column3: I've had my fill of meetings. Even my calendar looks tired.
column4: have had my fill of 在此表示已經受夠。

column3: We took the blows and kept our little business open.
column4: take the blows 指承受打擊，這裡仍努力經營。

column3: A free holiday? That sounds too good to be true.
column4: too good to be true 指好得令人難以置信。

column3: I sat beside a famous actor and asked his name.
column4: beside 表示在旁邊，這裡不知道鄰座是名人。

column3: We ran out of money after one ride at the fair.
column4: run out of 指用光，這裡很快花光錢。

column3: I called my boss “Mum” again. Yes, I did it again.
column4: do it again 表示再次做了同一件事。

column3: Are you serious? You invited the whole street?
column4: Are you serious? 用來確認令人驚訝的消息。

column3: You bought me flowers? You shouldn't have! Thank you!
column4: You shouldn't have! 可用來客氣地感謝別人的禮物。

column3: We drifted apart after moving to different cities.
column4: drift apart 指關係逐漸疏遠。

column3: This old photo means a lot to me.
column4: mean a lot to someone 指對某人很重要。

column3: I dived right in and joined the acting class.
column4: dive right in 表示毫不拖延地投入或開始。

column3: Follow my lead; copy these very silly dance steps.
column4: follow my lead 表示跟隨我的示範。

column3: Against all odds, Grandma won her first singing contest.
column4: against all odds 表示克服重重困難或在不被看好的情況下成功。

column3: In that old photo, we're frozen in time.
column4: frozen in time 指樣子像停留在過去，照片符合情境。

column3: He wanted to leave, so I let him go.
column4: let someone go 表示放手讓某人離開。

column3: I kept a poker face when my boss called me “Dad”.
column4: keep a poker face 表示不流露情緒，這裡忍住被叫錯稱呼的反應。

column3: My new haircut looks just like the mayor's. Help!
column4: just like 表示十分相似。

column3: He bluffed about knowing the answer. He had no idea.
column4: bluff 指假裝知道或有把握，以蒙混對方。

column3: I could read her face. She hated the new plan.
column4: read someone's face 指從表情看出心情。

column3: I love noise; she loves silence. We're worlds apart.
column4: worlds apart 形容兩者差異很大。

column3: I saw the crowd and changed my mind about singing.
column4: change your mind 表示改變主意。

column3: After the party, we went our separate ways.
column4: go separate ways 表示各自離開或走不同的路。

column3: I have no script; I make it up as I go.
column4: make it up as I go 表示一邊進行一邊即興編排。

column3: My ex and I dated last year. We're friends now.
column4: ex 指已結束戀愛關係的前任。

column3: This job is right for me; I love helping children.
column4: right for someone 表示適合某人。

column3: He cut me off before I finished my story.
column4: cut someone off 在此表示打斷別人說話。

column3: Grandma treats every visitor like a famous guest.
column4: treat someone like 表示以某種方式對待人。

column3: He's still hung up on his ex after three years.
column4: be hung up on someone 表示仍念念不忘某人。

column3: I know this theatre like the back of my hand.
column4: like the back of my hand 表示非常熟悉。

column3: Dad's glasses were beneath the newspaper he was reading.
column4: beneath 表示在下面。

column3: I used to live here, before the noisy band arrived.
column4: used to 表示過去的習慣或狀態，現在已有改變。

column3: I looked through the window and saw the wrong city.
column4: look through the window 表示透過窗戶往外看。

column3: My seat was gone. Grandpa was enjoying the view.
column4: be gone 表示已經沒有或不見了。

column3: This box holds keys, stamps and other odds and ends.
column4: odds and ends 指各種零碎的小物品。

column3: We're stuck in the lift. Dad has started singing.
column4: be stuck in 表示困在某處。

column3: I bought a couple of tickets. Grandma invited five friends.
column4: a couple of 指兩個或少數幾個；票數與邀請人數形成反差。

column3: We fold maps the same way: badly.
column4: the same way 表示用同樣方式，這裡打趣兩人都不會摺地圖。

column3: I made a mistake: my holiday photo reached the whole office.
column4: make a mistake 表示犯錯，這裡誤寄照片。

column3: Practice holds the key to winning this game.
column4: hold the key to 指掌握達成某事的關鍵。

column3: I want more time on stage. My family wants less.
column4: want more 表示想要更多，這裡與家人的反應形成對比。

column3: I am to blame. I gave the band our address.
column4: be to blame 表示應負責，這裡樂隊找到家門的原因是自己提供地址。

column3: This game has got a hold on me; I can't stop.
column4: get a hold on someone 在此指對某人有強大的吸引或控制力。
